# 0g.hk — full API reference

Minimal, no-login short URL + text note service on 0g.hk.
API version: 1
Abuse contact: abuse@0g.hk

This document is the canonical reference for machine clients (LLMs, scripts).
For a short cheat sheet see /llms.txt.

## Hosts

- 0g.hk           — apex, write API and editor UI
- <name>.0g.hk    — read API for an existing note (one subdomain per note name)

## Concepts

A note is identified by a `name` matching ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$
(lowercase letters, digits, hyphen; start and end with alnum).
The `content` is either:
- a URL (http/https, length <= 2048 bytes) → read returns 302 redirect, or
- arbitrary UTF-8 text (length <= 24576 bytes) → read returns the text.

Every successful create returns an `editToken` that must be presented to edit
or delete the note within its TTL.

The service does not store edit tokens in plaintext. If an edit token is lost,
it cannot be recovered from the public API or from KV metadata. A deployment
administrator who controls the Cloudflare KV namespace may issue a fresh edit
token by resetting the stored token hash for that note while preserving its
content and TTL.

## TTL

Accepted values: 1h, 1d, 7d. Default: 7d.
Notes are removed automatically when their TTL expires.

## Rate limit

Create / edit endpoints are limited to 10 requests per minute per client IP.
An adaptive limiter further reduces this to 2 req/min/ip after 5 rejected
requests in a short window.

## Endpoints

### POST/PUT https://0g.hk/

Create a note. Body may be:
- application/x-www-form-urlencoded with `c` (content), `n` (name), `ttl`, `token`
- application/json with `{ content, name, ttl, token }`
- text/plain — raw content; name auto-generated

Response 200 (JSON if Accept: application/json):
{
  "ok": true,
  "name": "demo",
  "url":  "https://demo.0g.hk/",
  "editUrl": "https://demo.0g.hk/edit",
  "editToken": "<32-char hex>",
  "expiresAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "ttl": "7d"
}

Response 200 (HTML if Accept: text/html): result page with name, short URL,
edit URL, editToken, copy buttons.

Response 4xx/5xx: see Error codes.

### GET https://0g.hk/

Non-browser (curl etc.) → returns this file's short companion (/llms.txt).
Browser → returns the editor page. With `?c=`, behaves like POST /.

### GET https://0g.hk/exists?n=<name>

Check whether a name is already taken.
Response: { "name": "...", "exists": true|false } (always 200).

### GET https://<name>.0g.hk/

Read a note.
- Browser + URL content: HTML interstitial showing the destination.
- Browser + text content: HTML rendering of the note (markdown when applicable).
- curl/JSON + URL content: 302 redirect to target.
- curl + text content: text/plain body.
- Accept: application/json: { name, content, contentType, expiresAt }.
- 404 if not found, 410 if disabled, 451 if abuse-flagged.

### GET https://<name>.0g.hk/raw

Returns the raw note body as text/plain regardless of UA. 404/410/451 as above.

### POST https://<name>.0g.hk/

Edit content. Body must include the `token` returned by create.
Application/json: { "content": "...", "token": "..." }.
Response 200: { ok, name, contentType, expiresAt }.

### POST https://<name>.0g.hk/edit

HTML edit form post-back. Body: form-urlencoded { content, token }.

The edit token may be sent three ways, all validated identically: the
`X-Edit-Token` request header, a `token` body field, or the deprecated
`?edit=<token>` query parameter. Prefer the first two — a query string is
recorded in Worker and Cloudflare request logs (where the value is now
redacted). `X-Edit-Token` is honoured on POST/PUT only; a GET carrying it is a
plain read.

### POST https://<name>.0g.hk/abuse

Report abuse. Body: { reason }, plus a Turnstile token as `turnstile` /
`cf-turnstile-response` (or the `X-Turnstile-Token` header) when the deployment
configures TURNSTILE_SECRET; an unverified report is rejected with
403 challenge_failed and changes no counter.

Reports are counted per REPORTER GROUP — one IPv6 /64 or one IPv4 /24 — so
varying the low bits of an address does not add to the count. After
ABUSE_AUTO_QUARANTINE (10) DISTINCT groups report a name, it is placed under a
bounded, reversible QUARANTINE (not a permanent disable): the marker lives for
the note's own remaining TTL, clamped to [1h, 7d], so it can never outlive the
content. A quarantined note answers 410 `disabled` with details.auto=true and
details.until. An admin can lift it immediately via POST /admin/enable.

## Headers

Every response includes:
- content-security-policy (strict)
- x-frame-options: DENY
- x-content-type-options: nosniff
- referrer-policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
- permissions-policy: geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=(), payment=()
- x-robots-tag: noindex, nofollow

Note read responses additionally include:
- x-note-name, x-note-content-type ("url" | "text"), x-note-expires-at

## Error codes

All error responses include a JSON body of shape
{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<human readable>" }
when Accept includes application/json or ?format=json is set.

400 invalid_request   — malformed body / params
400 invalid_name      — name fails NAME_RE
400 invalid_url       — content claims to be a URL but cannot be parsed
400 bad_scheme        — url scheme is not http/https
401 invalid_token     — editToken missing or wrong
403 reserved_name     — name is in RESERVED set
403 brand_blocked     — name contains a blocked brand substring
403 shortener_blocked — redirect target is itself a known shortener
404 not_found         — note does not exist or has expired
409 name_taken        — name already in use and not expired
410 gone              — note was disabled
413 too_large         — text > 24576 bytes or url > 2048 bytes
429 rate_limited      — over the per-minute create/edit limit
451 content_blocked   — moderation rejected the content
500 internal_error    — bug; please report with X-Request-Id if shown

## Reserved names

www api new admin edit raw n app abuse report exists
mail email dns mx ns cdn static assets help docs status

Plus all RFC 2606 reserved labels (example, invalid, localhost, test).

## Brand blocks

Names containing certain brand substrings (apple, google, paypal, binance,
openai, ...) are rejected as anti-phishing protection. The full list lives in
src/constants.ts (BRAND_BLOCK).

## Redirect target rules

When `content` is a URL we additionally enforce:
- scheme must be http or https
- host must not be in SHORTENER_HOSTS (chained shorteners are blocked)
- if the host is on REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST, redirect is direct (302)
- otherwise the read returns an HTML interstitial showing the destination
  before the user clicks through

## Quick examples

Create a text note:
  $ curl -s -X POST https://0g.hk/ -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"content":"hello","name":"hi","ttl":"1d"}'
  {"ok":true,"name":"hi","url":"https://hi.0g.hk/", ...}

Read it:
  $ curl -s https://hi.0g.hk/raw
  hello

Edit it:
  $ curl -s -X POST https://hi.0g.hk/ -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"content":"hi there","token":"<editToken>"}'
  {"ok":true,"name":"hi", ...}

Delete (set empty content):
  $ curl -s -X POST https://hi.0g.hk/ -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"content":"","token":"<editToken>"}'
